items.title: One non-model thing I'm very excited we announced today with Fable 5
items.text: One non-model thing I'm very excited we announced today with Fable 5.1 is Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS). Even if you're not a CEO/CISO, this blog post is a look into how big companies are thinking about AI adoption which is important to understand if you're interested in how AI might diffuse across industry. Companies are giving agents more and more access to internal systems. With traditional zero data retention, there's been no way to spot patterns in what agents might be doing across sessions on these systems. EFS is ZDR++. It's ZDR built for a world with agents. A company's data stays in its own cloud, and an automated monitoring layer we built flags risky patterns to its team. I...

items.title: AI for cyber is about to go vertical
items.text: AI for cyber is about to go vertical. The models increasingly becoming insanely good at finding and exploiting vulnerabilities. Frontier models are ahead, but we’re already seeing that open weights is not far behind. Most enterprises are already inundated with cyber discoveries, so now that’s only going to multiply. Triaging and automating the fixes with more AI -along with human oversight- is essentially the only way forward. In case you were wondering what jobs AI was going to create, it’s definitely going to great time to be in security.

I do manual iteration with AI to get it right 3. I then ask AI something like: "How would you update the skill so we can one-shot this?" before reviewing and approving its edits. The problem is AI often overfits on this one thread and over time the skill drifts. Any good solutions here?
